name: AI News Intelligence Digest (RSS + Postgres + Claude + Telegram)

parameters.content:
## AI News Intelligence Digest
Fetch RSS/Atom feeds every 2 hours, remove duplicates, group the same story from different sources, score it against your topics, summarize the best items with a small LLM (capped), and send a daily Telegram digest.

**Before running:**
1. Run sql/schema.sql (it seeds example feeds and topics)
2. Credentials: Postgres, Telegram, 'Anthropic API key' (Header Auth, name `x-api-key`)
3. Replace `REPLACE_WITH_DIGEST_CHAT_ID` (Telegram nodes) and `REPLACE_WITH_ALLOWED_CHAT_ID` (Code node *Parse Command*)
4. Set 'Error Workflow' in Workflow Settings to this workflow
5. Run 'Manual Fetch' once, then 'Manual Digest'

Manage feeds and topics from Telegram: /addfeed, /feeds, /follow.

### Dedupe, cluster, score
- Canonical URLs (tracking parameters removed) are unique in the database
- Titles are compared as word sets: Jaccard >= 0.6 and 3 shared words means the same story, even from another source. Matching looks back 72 hours
- Relevance = topic weight x keyword hits (title counts 3x). Articles older than 72 h are skipped, so a new feed does not flood you
- Only cluster founders above the relevance threshold are summarized, at most 15 per run and 3 attempts each

### Safety
Feed text is untrusted. The model only returns a tiny schema, has no tools, and its text is HTML-escaped before it reaches Telegram. /addfeed accepts only public http(s) URLs (no localhost, private ranges or credentials) and only the allowed chat can run commands.

parameters.query: SELECT id, name, url FROM feeds WHERE enabled ORDER BY id;

SELECT DISTINCT ON (title_norm) cluster_key, title_norm
FROM articles
WHERE fetched_at > now() - interval '72 hours'
ORDER BY title_norm, id;
SELECT name, keywords, weight FROM topics WHERE enabled ORDER BY id;

WITH input AS (
  SELECT * FROM json_to_recordset($1::json) AS x(
    feed_id int, canonical_url text, url text, title text, title_norm text, summary text,
    published_at timestamptz, cluster_key text, is_founder boolean, topic text, relevance numeric)
),
ins AS (
  INSERT INTO articles (feed_id, canonical_url, url, title, title_norm, summary, published_at,
                        cluster_key, is_founder, topic, relevance)
  SELECT feed_id, canonical_url, url, title, title_norm, summary, published_at,
         cluster_key, is_founder, topic, COALESCE(relevance, 0)
  FROM input
  ON CONFLICT (canonical_url) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING id
),
st AS (
  SELECT * FROM json_to_recordset($2::json) AS s(feed_id int, ok boolean, error text)
),
upd AS (
  UPDATE feeds f
  SET consecutive_failures = CASE WHEN st.ok THEN 0 ELSE f.consecutive_failures + 1 END,
      last_success_at      = CASE WHEN st.ok THEN now() ELSE f.last_success_at END,
      last_error           = CASE WHEN st.ok THEN NULL ELSE left(st.error, 300) END
  FROM st
  WHERE f.id = st.feed_id
  RETURNING f.name, f.last_error, f.consecutive_failures, st.ok
)
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*)::int FROM input) AS received,
       (SELECT COUNT(*)::int FROM ins)   AS inserted,
       COALESCE((SELECT json_agg(json_build_object('name', name, 'error', last_error))
                 FROM upd WHERE NOT ok AND consecutive_failures = $3::int), '[]'::json) AS newly_broken;

UPDATE articles a
SET summary_attempts = a.summary_attempts + 1
WHERE a.id IN (
  SELECT id FROM articles
  WHERE is_founder AND summarized_at IS NULL AND summary_attempts < 3
    AND relevance >= $1::numeric AND fetched_at > now() - interval '48 hours'
  ORDER BY relevance DESC, id
  LIMIT $2::int
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
)
RETURNING a.id, a.title, a.summary, a.topic;

UPDATE articles a
SET ai_summary = x.ai_summary, ai_importance = x.ai_importance, ai_category = x.ai_category, summarized_at = now()
FROM json_to_recordset($1::json) AS x(id bigint, ai_summary text, ai_importance int, ai_category text)
WHERE a.id = x.id
RETURNING a.id;

WITH win AS (
  SELECT a.*, f.name AS feed_name
  FROM articles a JOIN feeds f ON f.id = a.feed_id
  WHERE a.fetched_at > now() - interval '24 hours'
),
cl AS (
  SELECT cluster_key,
         COUNT(DISTINCT feed_id)::int AS sources_count,
         (ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT feed_name))[1:6] AS sources,
         MAX(relevance) AS relevance
  FROM win GROUP BY cluster_key
),
rep AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (cluster_key) cluster_key, title, url, topic, ai_summary, ai_importance
  FROM win
  ORDER BY cluster_key, (ai_summary IS NOT NULL) DESC, relevance DESC, published_at NULLS LAST, id
)
SELECT r.title, r.url, r.topic, r.ai_summary, r.ai_importance, c.sources_count, c.sources, c.relevance,
       ROUND((c.relevance + COALESCE(r.ai_importance, 0) + 2 * LN(c.sources_count))::numeric, 2) AS score
FROM cl c JOIN rep r USING (cluster_key)
WHERE c.relevance >= $1::numeric
ORDER BY score DESC, r.title
LIMIT $2::int;

INSERT INTO topics (name, keywords, weight)
VALUES ($1::text, ARRAY(SELECT json_array_elements_text($2::json)), 2)
ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET keywords = EXCLUDED.keywords, enabled = TRUE
RETURNING id, cardinality(keywords) AS n;
